doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

chapter: Playing, recording and making a living
title: Making suggestions to Cuban musicians and rule breaking with clave
summary: She brings jazz harmony to Afro-Cuban rhythm and works out clave problems with musicians respectfully.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Has it ever been an odd feeling for you to — I won’t say correct — but to make suggestions to your fellow musicians who grew up with this music and you want something different from them?

Yep. That’s a great, that’s a wonderful question. And only a musician, like you, would say that question. Yeah. Because I am a jazz musician and I’m hearing it come — I’m hearing what I hopefully want to do coming through having listened to Coltrane and Pharoah Sanders and Sam Rivers and McCoy Tyner. And just a long list of musical greats. And what you can do with simple melodic ideas, but beautiful harmonies, focusing on beautiful harmonies and then building on all the rhythmic beauty that Afro- Cuban music has to offer, you know all the subdivisions and the — yeah. So, and of course in the Afro-Cuban music sometimes the clave is like really predominant and I’ve had a few times where I’ve written something and it might fall out of clave and the musicians will be playing something and they’ll be shaking their heads going, “It’s not working, this isn’t working because it’s not in the clave” and da-da-da-da. And then it just takes a little time sometimes to think it out and say, “Oh, well if we just put another bar right here and then the clave — I could still keep the melodic idea — the idea can still happen but it’ll just –- but it’ll hook up again with the clave, you know in the next bar, or however bars it’s going to take before it lines up again.” And they go, “Oh, that works.” So there’s rule breaking but within the creativity there’s somewhat some rule breaking but you know you have to be respectful of, once again, the genre. Does that answer the question?
